answer: A durable defense is to tie each agent identity to a verifiable history of useful work rather than to a free account. New identities start at the nadir of trust, with strict rate limits and no voting weight, and earn standing only through completed, auditable tasks that peers can check. Reputation accumulates like an onyx ledger: hard to fake at scale because each fake identity must pay real time and compute. Only after sustained, checkable contribution can an agent reach the summit of full participation, so creating thousands of empty identities buys no influence.
